# Story 01 — Settings registry and configuration console (Story: 498)

## Prerequisites

- Story 2.2 (administrator authentication & role gating, tracked separately in `.squad/stories/inti/497/intake.md`) must expose a way to identify administrators and gate API/UI routes behind that role. If Story 2.2 has not yet produced middleware / a policy for the "Administrator" role, coordinate with its owner and land it first — this story assumes an `administrator` role gate exists.
- The Platform module (T0) already exists at `backend/app/Modules/Platform/` with `PlatformServiceProvider.php`, an established `Http/Middleware/` layer, `Support/` (utility) layer, and `Database/Migrations/` layout. All backend work in this story extends that module.
- Audit log write API from Story 2.4 (`.squad/stories/inti/499/intake.md`) is **blocked by this story** — do not depend on it. Emit an audit event via a **local interface** (`AuditLogger` contract) that ships with a no-op default; Story 2.4 will bind a real implementation.
- Tickets module (`backend/app/Modules/Tickets/`) currently contains only a `Domain/Placeholder.php`. This story is the first to add a real owned table (categories) there.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver the **settings registry** and the six-section **Configuration Console** so an Administrator can change runtime behaviour without a redeployment. Concretely:

1. A typed, validated settings store (table + per-module registry classes) with a cache that busts on write. Reading a setting **never** calls `config()` or `env()` outside boot.
2. A REST surface for administrators to read and write settings, list/create/update/delete/reorder **quick replies**, and manage the **flat ticket category list**.
3. A `Priority` PHP backed enum (string-backed) — not a table — with the four fixed values.
4. A Next.js console with six sections (Organisation, Ticketing, Service levels, Email, Platform, Audit log) plus a section index, an "immediate effect" write path, and destructive confirmations that name their consequence concretely.
5. Every setting change writes an audit-log entry (before → after) via the `AuditLogger` seam.
6. A lint / architecture test that fails the build if `env()` is called outside `config/`.

**Out of scope (visible in mockups but explicitly deferred):** Knowledge settings section, AI section, Portal & branding section, Integrations section, escalation-rule editor, auto-assignment editor, SLA policy scoping editor, channels beyond email. The Audit log section is a **placeholder tab** here — its data grid lands in Story 2.4.

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour:** there is no settings surface; runtime knobs live in `.env` / `config/`; the console does not exist; quick replies, categories, and priorities are not modelled.

**New behaviour:**

- Every administrator-changeable value is a **typed row** in `settings` with a declared **type**, **default**, and **validation rule**, registered by a per-module registry class.
- Runtime reads go through `SettingsRegistry::get('module.key')`. `config()` / `env()` are forbidden outside boot; a build-time check enforces this.
- Writes take effect immediately: the resolved-settings cache is busted synchronously in the same request that writes.
- Every write emits an audit-log entry with `before` and `after` values via the `AuditLogger` seam (no-op implementation in this story; Story 2.4 provides the real logger).
- **Quick replies** are a settings collection under key `tickets.quick_replies`: an ordered array of `{ id (ULID), label, body }` where `label` and `body` are both `{ en, ar }`. No owner user, no FK to a user, no per-agent variant, no variables/placeholders/template engine, no approval step, no versioning.
- **Categories** are rows in an owned Tickets table `ticket_categories` with columns `id`, `name_en`, `name_ar`, `sort_order`, timestamps, and **no** `parent_id` column. The list is flat by construction.
- **Priority** is a PHP 8.1+ string-backed enum `App\Modules\Tickets\Domain\Priority` with cases `Low = 'low'`, `Normal = 'normal'`, `High = 'high'`, `Urgent = 'urgent'`. The Priority section of the console displays these values as read-only and states that they are fixed.
- Destructive confirmations name the consequence concretely (e.g. "Delete the category 'Billing'. Tickets using it will …"). Rule-blocked actions return `409 Conflict` Problem Details with `count` and `path` fields so the UI can render "Cannot delete: 12 tickets still use it. See tickets → filter by category = Billing".

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Settings table and registry

**Create file:** `backend/database/migrations/2026_09_01_000100_create_settings_table.php`

Columns:

- `key` — string(191), primary key.
- `type` — string(32) (one of `bool`, `int`, `string`, `json`, `duration_seconds`, `enum`).
- `value` — `json` (nullable; use JSON for uniformity of encoding).
- `updated_by` — nullable FK to `users.id`.
- `updated_at` — timestamp with default `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` on update.
- `created_at` — timestamp.

Follow the filename + shape convention in `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Database/Migrations/2026_08_31_000100_create_idempotency_keys_table.php`. Publish via `PlatformServiceProvider` (see how the idempotency table is loaded).

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/SettingType.php`

```php
enum SettingType: string {
    case Bool = 'bool';
    case Int = 'int';
    case String = 'string';
    case Json = 'json';
    case DurationSeconds = 'duration_seconds';
    case Enum = 'enum';
}
```

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/SettingDefinition.php`

Immutable value object: `key`, `SettingType`, `default`, `validator` (Closure returning `true|string`), `allowedValues` (nullable, for `Enum`), `secret` (bool — masked in responses).

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/SettingsRegistry.php`

Public API:

```php
public function register(SettingDefinition $def): void;
public function all(): array; // key => resolved value (with defaults)
public function get(string $key): mixed;
public function set(string $key, mixed $value, ?int $actorUserId): array; // returns ['before' => …, 'after' => …]
public function definition(string $key): SettingDefinition;
public function knownKeys(): array;
```

Reads go through an in-memory cache seeded from `SettingsCache::resolved()`. `set()` validates, writes to the DB via `SettingsRepository::upsert()`, calls `SettingsCache::forget()`, then emits `AuditLogger::write(actor: …, action: 'settings.updated', target: $key, before: …, after: …)`.

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/SettingsRepository.php` — thin DB access (Eloquent or query builder) with `all()`, `find(string $key)`, `upsert(string $key, mixed $value, ?int $actor)`. No business rules.

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Settings/SettingsCache.php` — wraps Laravel `cache` store with a single key `platform:settings:resolved` and a TTL of one hour. `forget()` clears it; `resolved()` computes-and-stores when missing.

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Audit/AuditLogger.php`

```php
interface AuditLogger {
    public function write(?int $actorUserId, string $action, string $target, array $before, array $after): void;
}
```

**Create file:** `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Support/Audit/NullAuditLogger.php` — no-op implementation (Story 2.4 replaces the binding).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Writing an invalid value** — `SettingsRegistry::set` throws `ProblemException` (422); handled by `ProblemDetailsHandler` (`backend/app/Modules/Platform/Http/ProblemDetailsHandler.php`). UI shows inline validation.
- **Duplicate write race** — two admins PATCH the same key. Repository uses `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`; last-write-wins. Cache is busted after each write; a stale reader that read within the same 1-second window may see the previous value for at most one cache-fill.
- **Cache backend down** — `SettingsCache::resolved()` catches cache exceptions and falls back to a direct repository read; log a warning via `JsonContextProcessor`.
- **`env()` called at runtime** — build fails in `backend/tests/Architecture/NoEnvOutsideConfigTest.php`.
- **Rule-blocked category delete** — `DELETE /admin/categories/{id}` returns `409` Problem Details `{ type, title, count, path }`. UI renders concrete refusal, never a generic "cannot delete". In this story `count` is always `0` because tickets do not yet reference categories — but the enforcement path exists (a callable resolver in `TicketsServiceProvider`) so Story 5.x can plug in the real count query.
- **Quick reply id collision** — server generates ULIDs (`frontend/lib/api/ulid.ts` on client, PHP `Str::ulid()` server-side); reject client-supplied ids.
- **Bilingual field missing one language** — validator on `{en, ar}` shapes rejects missing keys with 422; UI marks the missing tab.
- **RTL rendering** — Arabic labels render right-to-left; use `BidiValue` (`frontend/components/domain/BidiValue/BidiValue.tsx`) for any preview of a quick-reply body.
- **Non-administrator hits admin route** — middleware returns 403; UI falls back to `ForbiddenState`.
- **Priority enum drift** — architecture test `backend/tests/Architecture/TierOrderingTest.php` already guards tier direction; add a unit test asserting `Priority::values() === ['low','normal','high','urgent']` so accidental case additions are caught.
- **Half-applied migration** — if only `settings` migrated but not `ticket_categories`, admin console loads but Categories panel returns 500. Migration order is deterministic by filename; document rollback below.
- **Uncertainty (mark for executor):** if Story 2.2 has **not** landed a `role:administrator` middleware alias when this story is executed, add the temporary stub described in section 3; do **not** invent a bespoke admin gate.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migrations must run in this order: `2026_09_01_000100_create_settings_table.php` → `2026_09_01_000200_create_ticket_categories_table.php`. Both are additive; no data backfill.
- **Rollback:** `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=2` drops both tables. No data loss beyond user-configured values (documented in the release note).
- **Half-applied state:** if only `settings` applied, category endpoints return 500 — admins should not see the Ticketing → Categories panel until both migrations succeed. Deploy migrations before shipping the frontend build.
- No config-file breaking changes. Any `config/*` keys copied into the registry retain their old `config/` values as **fallbacks in the definition's `default`** — removing them from `config/` is a follow-up (add a TODO comment referencing this story near each migrated key).

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** in `backend/`, run `composer install`, then `php artisan migrate:fresh` in a scratch env.
2. **Backend tests:** in `backend/`, run `./vendor/bin/phpunit` (or `php artisan test`). All Feature/Unit/Architecture suites must pass, including the new `NoEnvOutsideConfigTest`.
3. **Deptrac:** in `backend/`, run `./vendor/bin/deptrac analyse --config-file=deptrac.yaml` and `./vendor/bin/deptrac analyse --config-file=deptrac-tiers.yaml`. Zero violations.
4. **OpenAPI:** in `backend/`, run `php artisan openapi:check`. Must exit 0.
5. **Frontend runs:** in `frontend/`, run `pnpm install`, `pnpm dev`, and open `http://localhost:3000/admin` — verify the six-section index, all six pages render, PATCHing a Ticketing setting reflects in the UI without a reload.
6. **Frontend tests:** in `frontend/`, run `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint`. All new component tests, i18n parity, and lint rules pass.
7. **Regression:** existing tests in `backend/tests/Feature/Platform/*` and `frontend/__tests__/**` remain green.
8. **Manual — destructive confirmation copy:** delete a category, confirm the dialog names the category by name; delete a quick reply, confirm the dialog quotes its label.
9. **Manual — refusal:** with the category-in-use resolver stub set to return `count=3`, attempt delete → UI renders "Cannot delete: 3 tickets still use it" with a working link.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `settings` table exists; every administrator-changeable value is a typed row with declared type, default, and validation rule.
- [ ] Reads go through `SettingsRegistry`; no `config()` or `env()` call exists in `backend/app/` or `backend/routes/`; the architecture test enforces it.
- [ ] Writing a setting takes effect on the next read in the same process (cache busted synchronously) and emits an audit event via `AuditLogger`.
- [ ] The console has exactly six sections (Organisation, Ticketing, Service levels, Email, Platform, Audit log) with a persistent section index. No Knowledge / AI / Portal / Integrations section is rendered.
- [ ] Quick replies: create, edit, delete, reorder; bilingual label + body; no owner user, no per-agent variant, no placeholders/variables/template engine/approval/versioning.
- [ ] Categories: flat, `ticket_categories` table has no `parent_id`, CRUD works, delete is refused with `409` Problem Details `{ count, path }` when the resolver returns non-zero.
- [ ] `Priority` PHP string-backed enum exists with `Low · Normal · High · Urgent`; the Priorities section explicitly states they are fixed.
- [ ] Destructive confirmations name the consequence concretely; rule-blocked actions render a count + a path.
- [ ] `openapi.yaml` describes every new endpoint; `openapi:check` passes; frontend `schema.ts` is regenerated.
- [ ] All new + existing tests pass (`php artisan test`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `deptrac`, `openapi:check`).
